portrait noun

Traupman 169

imāgō, imāginis f.

noun, third declension

portrait, likeness (painted, drawn or sculpted)

A likeness of a person in any medium, with the genitive of the sitter (imāgō Āfricānī). Add picta for a painting, as against a bust or statue (ficta); imāginēs are also the wax masks of a Roman family’s ancestors. It has other common senses too: a reflection, an image in the mind, a ghost (see picture).

Other words

  • effigiēs, effigiēī f. — likeness, portrait, effigy

    noun, fifth declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.103: effigiēs hominis et imāgō (Lewis & Short)

    A copy that resembles its original, a likeness; more formal than imāgō.

Examples

  • similem esse tē volō quōmodo fīlium, nōn quōmodo imāginem: imāgō rēs mortua est

    I want you to resemble me as a son does, not as a portrait does: a portrait is a dead thingSen. Ep. 84.8

  • Hominum imāginēs pingere solet.

    He usually paints portraits.composed

See also picture, photo, represent, draw.

SourcesLewis & Short: imago · Lewis & Short: effigies
